title: The Uplift an Employer's Programme Allows for the Employee's Own Payment
content:
Where an employee has lately put money onto their own Employee Meal Account, the employer's dining programme allows an uplift on the share it picks up. The matched paydown uplift is 8 percent and the part paydown uplift is 4 percent.

**Clause.** Where value has been paid onto the account in the calendar month running back from the day the account is worked and the account has stood restricted for longer than the grace days printed against the plan, that uplift is the matched paydown uplift. Where value has been paid onto the account in the calendar month running back from the day the account is worked and the account has stood restricted for no longer than those grace days, that uplift is the part paydown uplift. Where neither holds, the uplift the employer's programme allows for the employee's own payment is nothing.

## The grace days this reads, plan by plan

| Meal plan | Grace after the arrears threshold is passed |
|---|---|
| Pay-As-You-Go Badge Account | 0 calendar days |
| Prepaid Declining Balance Account | 0 calendar days |
| Payroll Deduction Meal Account | 10 calendar days |
| Subsidized Daily Allowance Account | 7 calendar days |
| Full Subsidy Employee Meal Account | 0 calendar days |
| Executive Dining Charge Account | 21 calendar days |

## The bands

| Value paid onto the account in the calendar month running back from the day the account is worked | Days the restriction has stood | Uplift |
|---|---|---|
| Any amount above nothing | Longer than the printed grace days | 8 percent |
| Any amount above nothing | The printed grace days or fewer | 4 percent |
| None | Any | Nothing |

## Points of judgement

What is looked for is value paid onto the account within the calendar month running back from the day the account is worked; the size of that payment moves the uplift no further, and a payment older than that window allows none. A restriction standing for exactly the printed grace days is not longer than them and so takes the part uplift, while one standing a day more takes the matched uplift.

*Hypothetical illustration.* On a plan printing 10 calendar days of grace, an account loaded $40.00 twelve days into a restriction carries an uplift of 8 percent; loaded on the ninth day of that restriction it carries 4 percent; with no load in the calendar month running back from the day the account is worked it carries none.
